Adolescent wizard-in-training Harry Potter returns to Hogwarts for another year of schooling and learns more about the dark past of the boy who grew up to become Lord Voldemort in this, the sixth installment of the film series that originated from the writings of author J.K. Rowling. There was a time when Hogwarts was thought of as a safe haven, but thanks to Voldemort's tightening grip on both the Muggle and wizarding worlds, that simply isn't the case anymore. Suspecting that the castle may even harbor an outright threat, Harry finds his investigation into the matter sidelined by Dumbledore's attempts to prepare him for the monumental battle looming ever closer on the horizon. In order to discover the key to Voldemort's defenses, Dumbledore enlists the aid of resourceful yet unsuspecting bon vivant Professor Horace Slughorn, who may have a clue as to their enemy's Achilles' heel. Meanwhile, teenage hormones cause the students at Hogwarts to lose focus on their true mission. As Harry and Dean Thomas clash for the affections of the lovely Ginny, Romilda Vane attempts to woo Ron away from Lavender Brown with some particularly tasty chocolates. Even Hermione isn't immune from the love bug, though she tries her hardest to suppress her growing jealousy and keep her emotions bottled up. But there is one student who remains completely aloof from the romance blossoming all around, and he intends to leave a dark impression on his classmates. With tragedy looming ever closer, it begins to appear as if peace will prove elusive in Hogwarts for some time to come.

snippet.title: The Impending Death of Albus Dumbledore | Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
snippet.description:
"Severus, please."

Draco Malfoy (Tom Felton) leads fellow Death Eaters, including Bellatrix Lestrange (Helena Bonham Carter) into Hogwarts to assassinate Professor Dumbledore (Michael Gambon). 
 
As Lord Voldemort tightens his grip on both the Muggle and wizarding worlds, Hogwarts is no longer a safe haven. Harry suspects perils may even lie within the castle, but Dumbledore is more intent upon preparing him for the final battle fast approaching. Together they work to find the key to unlock Voldemort’s defenses and to this end, Dumbledore recruits his old friend and colleague Horace Slughorn, whom he believes holds crucial information. Even as the decisive showdown looms, romance blossoms for Harry, Ron, Hermione and their classmates. Love is in the air, but danger lies ahead and Hogwarts may never be the same again.

At the same time, Dumbledore prepares Harry for the final battle, revealing important secrets to him.

Description of actors and their roles:

Daniel Radcliffe as Harry Potter: Harry continues to fight the growing threat of Voldemort, exploring his past and uncovering the secrets of The Half-Blood Prince.

Emma Watson as Hermione Granger: Hermione remains Harry's loyal friend and supports him on his missions while experiencing the complex emotions associated with Ron.

Rupert Grint as Ron Weasley: Harry's best friend who faces problems in his personal relationships and becomes part of a love triangle with Hermione.

Michael Gambon as Albus Dumbledore: Director of Hogwarts, who reveals to Harry important details from Voldemort's past and prepares him for the final battle.

Alan Rickman as Severus Snape: A Hogwarts professor whose loyalty remains mysterious, and he is also the Half-Blood Prince, the owner of a book that plays a key role in the film.

Tom Felton as Draco Malfoy: A Slytherin student who receives a dangerous assignment from Voldemort and becomes one of the key figures in the development of events.

Jim Broadbent as Horace the Slug: A new pooling teacher whom Harry uses to learn important information about Voldemort.

"Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince" combines mystical and emotional themes, delving into Voldemort's past, revealing secrets that will pave the way for a decisive battle between good and evil.

snippet.title: Funny Harry Potter set anecdotes you probably never knew about! #harrypotter
snippet.description: Lots of fun behind‑the‑scenes stories happened during the Harry Potter filming. The slugs Ron vomited were sweet‑tasting studio slime, which Rupert Grint enjoyed and tried to get Emma and Daniel to taste, though they refused. Michael Gambon played a fart‑prank device inside Daniel’s sleeping bag during a Great Hall scene, making young cast members struggle not to laugh and ruining multiple shots. In *Goblet of Fire*, teenage actors went through puberty; many Hogwarts students wore longer hair to hide acne and physical changes. In the first film’s ending, shy Emma Watson felt awkward hugging boys, so the scene was adjusted — she hugged Harry and shook Ron’s hand instead. Before Voldemort’s actor was announced, Rupert Grint firmly believed Mr Bean would take the role and told everyone about it. Do you know how many wands Daniel Radcliffe broke throughout filming?
